::: {.tagline}
Political economist. Senior United Nations official. Quantitative social scientist.
:::

For more than a decade I have served the United Nations in some of its most demanding duty stations: Jerusalem, Baghdad, Kabul, Amman, Nicosia, Beirut, and Pristina. I have led multinational teams through war and crisis, advised under-secretaries-general and assistant secretaries-general, facilitated negotiations alongside UN mediators, worked with ambassadors, and co-led international assessments that put a number on the cost of war. Through all of it runs a single conviction: rigorous analysis, honestly communicated, improves decisions when the stakes are highest.

I am a political scientist by training (Ph.D., UC Berkeley) and a quantitative social scientist by practice. I currently serve as the senior economist for the United Nations in Kosovo.

More about my work on the [About](about.qmd) page. Selected research and reports under [Research & Publications](publications.qmd).
